title: An invitation opened while signed in with another address offers a sign-out-and-sign-in button instead of a link that loops back to the same refusal
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout, with no database: env -u TEST_DATABASE_URL node --test apps/tracy-web/test/invite-account-switch.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/seats-pages.test.mjs
S2: Read the pass/fail counts and the test named '#799: the action on the wrong-account page leads to the sign-in door, not back to the refusal'.
expect: GET /invite/<token> for a viewer signed in with an address other than the invited one answers 403 and sets no cookie.

The page's one action is <form method="post" action="/auth/signout"> with a single hidden field next = /login?next=%2Finvite%2F<token>&email=<invited address> and one submit button labelled 'Sign in as <invited address>'; the form has no data-fetch attribute and the page holds no link to /login.

Posting the form's own fields answers 303 to <origin>/login?next=%2Finvite%2F<token>&email=<invited address> and deletes tracy_sess, tracy_site and every tracy_tok_* cookie; following it with the emptied jar answers 200 with the invited address in the email field and next pointing at /invite/<token>.

The refusal runs exactly one statement (the rate_bucket upsert keyed invite-accept:<token>); a foreign-origin or wrong-body-type sign-out post is refused (403 CSRF_ORIGIN / 415) and clears nothing; an off-origin next is redirected to this origin.
Before the fix (seats/pages.js at 83eaff46f): the action was <a class="back" href="/login?next=…">; following it answered 302 to /invite/<token> and then the same 403 (7 failures in these two files).
evidence: apps/tracy-web/test/invite-account-switch.test.mjs (the real seats and identity routers behind csrfGuard, in one process; the pool answers only the rate_bucket upsert); apps/tracy-web/test/seats-pages.test.mjs (markup, escaping, eight languages).
fence: In-process only: no database, no browser and no deployed host. Accepting the invitation after signing in as the invited address (ensureAccount, acceptGrant) is not exercised by this case, and cookie Domain/Secure/SameSite behaviour in a real browser is not modelled.
